corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN, with less novelty than the checker claimed. The closed-walk/cover comparison is known (Cioaba 2006; FMT 2006). A WEIGHTED version, for arbitrary nonnegative weights on K frequencies, is also already known: Wang-Ye arXiv:2503.06908 Thm 4.6/Prop 4.5 gives m(y) <= [2p sin^2(pi/2m)/(p-(m-1)^K)] ||y||_1. What is new is only the support-size-free bound under the concave l_{1/s} budget (m(y) <= C (ln p)^{1-s} for every feasible y) and K >= c_s ln p, obtained by the Bessel exponential-moment route.
issues: Both confirmed citations check out: I fetched the PDFs, converted them to text and read them. Cioaba CRAS 342 (2006) 635-638: eq. (2) and Lemma 2.1 say what the checker says; leave the issue number out. FMT JCTB 96(1) (2006) 111-121: the abstract, the Sec. 3 covering argument and the folklore remark are as described. One small error: FMT's pointer is AR94 Proposition 3, Sec. 3, not Prop. 2 as CHECK.md says. MISSED PRIOR ART: Wang & Ye, arXiv:2503.06908 (2025). The checker read only its abstract and called it adjacent. It is the closest precedent. For any positive definite f on a finite abelian group, Thm 4.6 and Prop 4.5 lower-bound the second-largest value by a Fourier-analytic generalized covering argument (Sec. 4.1). Take f = sum_j y_j cos(2 pi j delta/p) on Z_p (t=0, r=K). Then it reads m(y) <= [2p sin^2(pi/2m)/(p-(m-1)^K)] ||y||_1, i.e. m(y) = O(||y||_1 p^{-2/K}) for ARBITRARY nonnegative weights. Prop 4.11 covers weighted Cayley graphs; Prop 5.5 covers relaxation time for any probability measure with support <= s. Remark 5.6 cites earlier weighted and probabilistic versions (Greenhalgh 1989; Hough EJP 2017; Hermon-Olesker-Taylor AAP 2023); I did not fetch these. So the checker's claims 'the published results are for fixed degree with unit weights' and 'what is new here is the weighted version' are false. The recommended sentence would overclaim. Replace its last sentence: cite Wang-Ye alongside FMT, and restrict the novelty to the support-free bound under the concave budget sum y_j^{1/s} <= 1 plus its log p consequence. My own derivation, not a citation: since r<1 gives ||y||_1 <= 1, Wang-Ye Thm 4.6 alone gives only K >~ ln p/ln ln p and no bound uniform in K. Their variable-radius Prop 4.5 might reproduce eq:Kbound up to constants; I did not check this. The Chowla/Bourgain/Ruzsa/Sanders line is correctly excluded, because the direction is opposite. The unit-weight statement also follows from Dirichlet pigeonhole / Bohr-set size (Tao-Vu Lemma 4.20), but I fetched no source for it. extra_citations.why: Closest precedent, and weighted. Thm 4.6 / Prop 4.5 (Sec. 4.1, 'a generalized covering argument', Fourier-analytic) bound nu_1(f)-nu_2(f) <= 4|G| sum_i fhat(chi_i) sin^2(pi/2m_i)/(|G|-2^t prod(m_i-1)) for every positive definite f. On Z_p with f = sum_j y_j cos(2 pi j delta/p) this is m(y) = O(||y||_1 p^{-2/K}) for arbitrary nonnegative weights on K frequencies. Prop 4.11 applies it to weighted abelian Cayley graphs and Prop 5.5 to random-walk relaxation times. Cite it next to friedman2006spectral at eq:posfourier. The novelty claim must then be restricted to the support-free, budget-normalised bound and its log p consequence.
